question: It has been brought to light that Russian oil that should be subject to sanctions is being imported on unmarked boats into the Croatian port of Ploče via its international terminal. Companies from Bosnia and Herzegovina then buy up the oil and distribute it onwards as their own throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina and on to Croatia and Europe.

The whole operation is reportedly unfolding under the protection of the political elite in Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, in particular the Croatian Democratic Union in Croatia and the Croatian Democratic Union in Bosnia and Herzegovina. In this way, such structures and other elements of organised crime stand to make a lot of money. 1.
Does the Commission have any information about the import or traffic of Russian oil through Croatia?
Does it have any information about the transport of Russian oil via the port of Ploče?
answer: The implementation of EU sanctions is Member States’ responsibility. The Commission monitors such compliance and is in regular contact with Member States’ national competent authorities regarding allegations of breaches. The Commission does not have any information on the alleged violation of sanctions as outlined by the Honourable Member. It will ensure adequate follow-up, including outreach to Croatia, in order to receive additional information on the matter.
